text:
TF-IDF clustering is inexpensive and useful for catalog similarity, but lexical coherence alone does not establish sustained user preference. Adobe’s recommender uses cosine similarity over modified TF-IDF catalog vectors; scikit-learn’s text-clustering example removes headers, signatures and quotations to reduce distracting metadata. Applied to Amazon titles/descriptions, this suggests a plausible shortcut: clusters driven by repeated brand names, model identifiers or boilerplate rather than interests. This is a hypothesis to test, not an established finding for these four datasets. [Adobe documentation](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/target/using/recommendations/criteria/recommendations-algorithms), [scikit-learn example](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/text/plot_document_clustering.html).

Stability is insufficient evidence: consensus-clustering experiments recovered apparently stable clusters from unimodal data without genuine groups. Cheap proposed controls: compare title-only versus description-only clusters; remove repeated phrases and brand-like tokens observed in available text; inspect top terms and near-duplicate concentration; measure adjusted Rand agreement across seeds and subsamples. For behavioral evidence, permute item-to-text assignments within each dataset while preserving histories and item frequencies; separately shuffle each history’s order to test temporal persistence, recognizing that this preserves overall lexical preference. Compare observed effects with these null distributions and judge recommendation usefulness by the unchanged macro validation HR@10. Sparse TF-IDF plus MiniBatchKMeans is straightforward; designing nulls that preserve relevant catalog structure requires more care. Treat clusters as candidate content features until predictive gains survive ablations and controls. [Consensus-clustering study](https://www.nature.com/articles/srep06207), [scikit-learn implementation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/auto_examples/text/plot_document_clustering.html).
